section_type: Energy Intake (Calories) by Age, Sex, Activity

text:
Macronutrients - Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (AMDR)

**Source:** Dietary Guidelines / National Academies. 

- **Carbohydrates:** 45–65% of total calories.  
- **Protein:** 10–35% of total calories.  
- **Fat:** 20–35% of total calories.  
  - **Saturated fat:** <10% of calories.  
  - **Trans fat:** as low as possible.

section_type: Macronutrients - Protein (grams per kg body weight)
text:
Macronutrients - Protein (grams per kg body weight)

- **General adult RDA:** 0.8 g/kg/day.   
- **Older adults (65+):** 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day to prevent sarcopenia.   
- **Active / strength training:** 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day depending on goals.   
  - Muscle gain / intense training: up to 1.6–2.4 g/kg/day. 

**Example:** 80 kg moderately active male → 0.8–1.2 g/kg → 64–96 g protein/day baseline; if training hard, 96–160 g/day.

Macronutrients - Fiber

**Source:** Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020–2025. 

**Recommended Daily Fiber (grams/day)**

| Age     | Women | Men  |
|---------|-------|------|
| 19–30   | 28 g  | 34 g |
| 31–50   | 25 g  | 31 g |
| 51+     | 22 g  | 28 g |

- Alternate rule: **14 g fiber per 1,000 kcal** consumed.

Macronutrients - Added Sugar

**Sources:** AHA, WHO, Dietary Guidelines. 

- **AHA:**  
  - Women: ≤25 g/day (~6 tsp, ~100 kcal).  
  - Men: ≤36 g/day (~9 tsp, ~150 kcal).  
- **Dietary Guidelines:** <10% of total calories from added sugar.  
  - For 2,000 kcal: <50 g/day.  
- **WHO:**  
  - Strong: <10% of calories.  
  - Conditional/ideal: <5% of calories (~25 g on 2,000 kcal).

Macronutrients - Fats: Omega-3 (EPA+DHA)

**Sources:** AHA, NIH ODS, FDA. 

- **General healthy adults:** 250–500 mg/day combined EPA+DHA (≈2 servings fatty fish/week).   
- **Known coronary heart disease:** ~1,000 mg/day EPA+DHA.   
- **High triglycerides:** 2–4 g/day EPA+DHA under medical supervision.   
- **FDA upper limit:** ≤3 g/day total EPA+DHA, with ≤2 g/day from supplements. 

**ALA (plant omega-3):**  
- Men: 1.6 g/day.  
- Women: 1.1 g/day.

Micronutrients (Vitamins & Minerals) - Sodium & Potassium

**Sources:** National Academies, AHA/ACC 2025, Dietary Guidelines. 

- **Sodium:**  
  - General limit: <2,300 mg/day.  
  - Ideal for BP control (especially hypertension): ~1,500 mg/day. 
- **Potassium (AI):**  
  - Men: ~3,400 mg/day.  
  - Women: ~2,600 mg/day.  
  - For hypertension: AHA suggests 3,500–5,000 mg/day if kidney function is normal.

Hydration

**Source:** National Academies of Sciences (DRI for Water). 

**Total Water (from all beverages + food)**

- **Men (19+):** 3.7 L/day (~125 oz; ~13 cups of fluids).  
- **Women (19+):** 2.7 L/day (~91 oz; ~9 cups of fluids).  

Approx. 20% typically comes from food; the rest from drinks. 

> Adjust upward for heat, high altitude, heavy exercise, pregnancy, lactation.

Physical Activity & Movement - Aerobic Activity (Adults 18–64)

- **Minimum:**  
  - 150–300 min/week moderate-intensity **or**  
  - 75–150 min/week vigorous-intensity **or**  
  - Equivalent combination.  
- **Additional benefits:** >300 min moderate or >150 min vigorous per week.

Physical Activity & Movement - Muscle-Strengthening

- **At least 2 days/week**, moderate or greater intensity, involving all major muscle groups.

Physical Activity & Movement - Older Adults (65+)

- Same aerobic minimums as above.  
- Add **multicomponent activity** (balance + strength) ≥3 days/week to prevent falls.

section_type: Physical Activity & Movement - Steps per Day
text:
Physical Activity & Movement - Steps per Day

Evidence-based observational data (not a formal guideline but widely used):

- **Sedentary:** <5,000 steps/day.  
- **General health:** 7,000–10,000 steps/day associated with lower mortality.  
- **Higher fitness/weight loss:** 10,000–12,000+ steps/day often used.

Heart Rate Zones for Exercise

**Sources:** Cleveland Clinic, Healthline, ACSM-based tables. 

**Estimate Max Heart Rate (HRmax):**  

\[
\text{HR}_{\text{max}} \approx 220 - \text{age}
\]

**Common 5-Zone Model (% of HRmax):**

- **Zone 1 (very light):** <57%  
- **Zone 2 (light):** 57–63%  
- **Zone 3 (moderate/vigorous):** 64–76%  
- **Zone 4 (hard):** 77–95%  
- **Zone 5 (maximal):** 96–100%  

Another common practical model:

- Zone 1: 50–60%  
- Zone 2: 60–70%  
- Zone 3: 70–80%  
- Zone 4: 80–90%  
- Zone 5: 90–100% 

Use these to prescribe cardio intensity (e.g., “spend most steady-state cardio in Zone 2”).

Sleep

**Sources:** National Sleep Foundation, CDC, sleep medicine consensus.

**Recommended Sleep Duration**

- **Adults (18–64):** 7–9 hours/night.  
- **Older adults (65+):** 7–8 hours/night.

**Sleep Architecture (typical healthy adult, approximate % of total sleep)**

- **N1 (light):** 2–5%  
- **N2:** 45–55%  
- **N3 (deep/slow-wave):** 13–23%  
- **REM:** 20–25%  

Good sleep quality: falling asleep within ~30 min, ≤1 awakening, total wake time <20 min after sleep onset.

Body Composition & Anthropometrics - BMI Categories (Adults)

**Source:** WHO/CDC.

- **Underweight:** <18.5 kg/m²  
- **Normal:** 18.5–24.9  
- **Overweight:** 25.0–29.9  
- **Obese Class I:** 30.0–34.9  
- **Obese Class II:** 35.0–39.9  
- **Obese Class III:** ≥40.0  

Use with caution in very muscular or elderly populations.

section_type: Body Composition & Anthropometrics - Waist Circumference (Abdominal Obesity)
text:
Body Composition & Anthropometrics - Waist Circumference (Abdominal Obesity)

Common cutoffs (ethnicity-specific nuances exist):

- **Men:** >102 cm (40 in) increased risk.  
- **Women:** >88 cm (35 in) increased risk.  

Lower cutoffs for some Asian populations (~90 cm men, 80 cm women).

Clinical Biomarkers (Blood & Vitals) - Blood Pressure (Adults)

**Source:** ACC/AHA guidelines.

- **Normal:** <120/<80 mmHg  
- **Elevated:** 120–129/<80  
- **Stage 1 Hypertension:** 130–139 / 80–89  
- **Stage 2 Hypertension:** ≥140 / ≥90

section_type: Clinical Biomarkers (Blood & Vitals) - Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c
text:
Clinical Biomarkers (Blood & Vitals) - Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c

- **Fasting glucose:**  
  - Normal: <100 mg/dL  
  - Prediabetes: 100–125 mg/dL  
  - Diabetes: ≥126 mg/dL (on two tests)  
- **HbA1c:**  
  - Normal: <5.7%  
  - Prediabetes: 5.7–6.4%  
  - Diabetes: ≥6.5%

Clinical Biomarkers (Blood & Vitals) - Lipid Panel (Adults)

**Sources:** MedlinePlus, MSD Manuals, AHA/ATP III. 

| Marker              | Optimal / Desirable                         | Borderline                         | High / Risk                          |
|---------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Total cholesterol   | <200 mg/dL                                  | 200–239                            | ≥240                                 |
| LDL cholesterol     | <100 mg/dL (<70 if high risk)               | 100–129 (130–159 borderline high)  | ≥160 (≥190 very high)                |
| HDL cholesterol     | ≥60 mg/dL (protective)                      | 40–59 (men), 50–59 (women)         | <40 (men), <50 (women) = low         |
| Triglycerides       | <150 mg/dL                                  | 150–199                            | ≥200 (≥500 very high)                |

Clinical Biomarkers (Blood & Vitals) - Cortisol (Stress Hormone)

**Sources:** MedlinePlus, WebMD, functional ranges. 

**Serum cortisol (blood):**

- **Morning (7–9 AM):** ~5–25 µg/dL (140–690 nmol/L); optimal often cited ~10–18 µg/dL.  
- **Afternoon (~4 PM):** ~3–16 µg/dL.  
- **Late night:** <5 µg/dL.

Interpretation depends on assay, time, and clinical context.

Substance Intake Limits - Alcohol

**Sources:** NIAAA, Dietary Guidelines. 

**Low-risk limits (per day, not averages):**

- **Women:** ≤1 drink/day; ≤7/week.  
- **Men:** ≤2 drinks/day; ≤14/week.  

**Heavy drinking:**

- **Women:** ≥4 drinks on any day or ≥8/week.  
- **Men:** ≥5 drinks on any day or ≥15/week.

1 drink ≈ 14 g pure alcohol (12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, 1.5 oz spirits).

Substance Intake Limits - Caffeine

**Sources:** EFSA, FDA, ACOG, WHO. 

- **Healthy adults:** up to **400 mg/day** total.  
- **Single dose:** up to **200 mg** at once is generally safe.  
- **Pregnant/breastfeeding:** ≤200 mg/day (some bodies say ≤300 mg).

Sedentary Behavior & Screen Time

**Sources:** WHO 2020 guidelines. 

- **Adults:** “Limit the amount of time spent being sedentary”; replace with any-intensity movement.  
- No strict hour limit for adults, but higher sedentary time is linked to higher mortality and CVD/diabetes risk.  
- For children, WHO gives specific screen limits (e.g., ≤1 hour/day for 2–4y), but for adults the guidance is qualitative: break up long sitting every 30–60 minutes.

Intermittent Fasting (IF) Protocols

**Sources:** NIA, PMC reviews on IF. 

Common IF regimens:

- **Time-Restricted Eating (TRE):**  
  - 16:8 (16 h fast, 8 h eating window) most common.  
  - 14:10, 18:6, 20:4 also used.  
- **5:2 diet:** 5 normal days, 2 non-consecutive “fast” days at ~500–600 kcal or ~20–25% of needs.   
- **Alternate-Day Fasting (ADF):** Alternating “fast” days (~25% of energy) with normal days.

**Observed effects (short to medium term):**

- Weight loss: ~3–8% over 8–12 weeks, similar to continuous calorie restriction.   
- Improvements in insulin sensitivity, fasting glucose, triglycerides, sometimes BP.   

**Notes:**

- Not for everyone: caution in pregnancy, underweight, eating disorders, certain medical conditions.  
- Protein and micronutrient adequacy must still be met within eating windows.

Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based Basics) - Creatine Monohydrate

- **Dose:** 3–5 g/day.  
- **Benefits:** Strength, power, lean mass, cognitive support in some populations.  
- Safe long-term in healthy adults with normal kidney function.

Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based Basics) - Vitamin D

- If sun exposure is low or levels are low: often 1,000–2,000 IU (25–50 µg)/day, adjusted to keep 25(OH)D in sufficient range per clinician guidance.

section_type: Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based Basics) - Omega-3 (if not eating fish)
text:
Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based Basics) - Omega-3 (if not eating fish)

- **General health:** 250–500 mg EPA+DHA/day.  
- **Heart disease:** ~1,000 mg/day (under guidance).

Supplements (Optional, Evidence-Based Basics) - Probiotics

- No universal RDA; typical supplements: 1–10 billion CFU/day, strain-specific effects.  
- Best used for specific indications (antibiotic-associated diarrhea, some IBS subtypes), not as a blanket “must.”

Special Populations (Quick Modifiers) - Pregnancy

- **Calories:** +340 kcal/day (2nd trimester), +450 kcal/day (3rd).  
- **Protein:** ~1.1 g/kg/day (varies by guideline).  
- **Folate:** 600 µg DFE/day.  
- **Iron:** 27 mg/day.  
- **Iodine:** 220 µg/day.  
- **Caffeine:** ≤200 mg/day.

Special Populations (Quick Modifiers) - Lactation

- **Calories:** +450–500 kcal/day.  
- **Protein:** ~1.3 g/kg/day (varies).  
- **Folate:** 500 µg DFE/day.  
- **Iodine:** 290 µg/day.  
- **Omega-3:** ~1,000 mg DHA+EPA/day recommended by some groups.

Special Populations (Quick Modifiers) - Older Adults (65+)

- **Protein:** 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day (up to 1.5 g/kg if frail/ill).   
- **Vitamin D & Calcium:** prioritize for bone health.  
- **Activity:** include balance training ≥3 days/week.
